# Disagreement Log — Didache Chapter 6

**Date:** 2026-03-17
**Chapter:** Didache 6 — Warning and Food Laws
**Agents:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA

---

## Summary
Total disagreements: 4

---

## Disagreement 1 — v.1: πλανήσῃ — "leads astray" vs. "causes to err"

| Agent | Rendering |
|-------|-----------|
| EMET | "causes you to err" |
| LOGOS | "leads you astray" |
| PNEUMA | "tries to lead you away" |

**Issue:** πλανάω = to lead astray, cause to wander (same root as πλάνος, "deceiver," used in ch. 16). LOGOS captures the active deceptive quality better.
**Ruling:** "Leads you astray" (LOGOS) adopted.

---

## Disagreement 2 — v.2: τέλειος — "perfect" vs. "complete"

| Agent | Rendering |
|-------|-----------|
| EMET | "you will be perfect" |
| LOGOS | "you will be perfect" |
| PNEUMA | "you'll be complete" |

**Issue:** Recurring term. EMET and LOGOS use "perfect"; PNEUMA uses "complete." Previous rulings in chs. 1 and 3 have adopted "complete" for τέλειος.
**Ruling:** "Complete" adopted for consistency with established ruling.

---

## Disagreement 3 — v.3: Structure — general accommodation then specific prohibition

| Agent | Rendering |
|-------|-----------|
| EMET | Presents both rules in parallel |
| LOGOS | Same parallel structure |
| PNEUMA | Explicitly flags the prohibition as "not negotiable" |

**Issue:** PNEUMA adds an interpretive gloss not present in the Greek. However, the structural logic it identifies is correct: the idol-food prohibition stands apart from the general food accommodation.
**Ruling:** LOGOS structure retained without the gloss. The structure itself makes the distinction clear.

---

## Disagreement 4 — v.3: "dead gods" — full phrase rendering

| Agent | Rendering |
|-------|-----------|
| EMET | "worship of dead gods" |
| LOGOS | "worship of dead gods" |
| PNEUMA | "worship of dead gods" |

**Issue:** All three agents agree on this striking phrase. No disagreement — but the council notes the theological significance: this is a specific claim that pagan deities are dead, not merely non-existent. Unanimous agreement to preserve the phrase exactly.
**Ruling:** "Worship of dead gods" — unanimous.
